name: IEC AND gate (rectangular form)
summary: Rectangular IEC-style AND element marked with an ampersand; the output is active only when every input is active.
description: The IEC rectangular AND element is a plain box with the ampersand written near the top centre. Inputs enter on the left and the single output leaves on the right, so the function is identified by the qualifier rather than by the outline shape. All inputs must stand at their internal 1 state for the output to take its internal 1 state.

Rectangular gates are common on European interlock, burner-management and protection logic sheets because the same box can carry negation circles, polarity indicators and dependency labels without changing shape. A drafter can stack several & boxes in one column and the function remains readable even when the elements are abutted.

The qualifier says nothing about logic family, supply voltage, propagation delay or whether the function is realised in hardware, relay contacts or PLC code. Those details come from the device schedule or the software reference attached to the sheet.
readingNotes: Read the & qualifier first; the box outline is identical for most IEC combinative elements.
Check for negation circles or polarity triangles on inputs before writing the truth table.
drawingChecklist: Show the & qualifier clearly inside the outline.
Number each input when more than two are used.
Reference the implementing device, PLC block or relay logic on the sheet.
distinction: The ≥1 OR element uses the same box; only the qualifier differs, so a misread character changes the whole function.
